web.no_docker: Docker is not available. Re-run the install command (it installs Docker).
web.not_installed: The web stack is not installed yet; it is installed with your first site (uses ports 80 / 443).
web.cf_token_hint: Permissions: Zone → DNS → Edit and Zone → Zone → Read; for firewall sync also Zone → Firewall Services → Edit, and Zone → Zone Settings → Edit to change the security level. Stored encrypted and never shown again.
web.acme_directory_hint: From your LiteSSL / CA dashboard, together with the EAB key ID and HMAC key.
web.tos: Requesting a certificate accepts the selected CA's terms of service.

site.php_switch_hint: Takes effect immediately; a version used for the first time takes a few minutes to build.
site.dns_hint: Creates A (IPv4) and AAAA (IPv6) records pointing to this server
site.need_cf: Set a Cloudflare API token under Web stack first
site.ssl_http_hint: The domain must already point to this server (port 80 reachable)
site.ssl_dns_hint: Validated via Cloudflare TXT records; supports wildcards
site.ssl_disable_confirm: Remove this site's certificate and turn off Force HTTPS?
site.cf_hint_title: The domain is proxied by Cloudflare (orange cloud)
site.cf_hint_dns: Use DNS-01 (Cloudflare) instead, which is not affected by the proxy; or temporarily set Cloudflare SSL/TLS mode to Full (not strict) and switch back to Full (strict) once issued.
site.cf_hint_token: Cloudflare rejects the origin until it has a valid certificate (526 in Full (strict) mode). Easiest: add a Cloudflare API token under Web stack and request with DNS-01; or temporarily set SSL/TLS mode to Full (not strict).
site.need_runtime: Install this runtime from the App Store first.
site.app_port_hint: The app listens on 127.0.0.1:PORT (env PORT / HOST)
site.command_hint: Runs in the project directory with sh -c; empty = default for the runtime
site.proxy_target_hint: http(s)://host:port, e.g. a Docker container on 127.0.0.1
site.passthrough: TLS passthrough (the backend holds the certificate)
site.passthrough_hint: host:port of a TLS backend; HTTP redirects to HTTPS
site.composer_hint: Runs Composer in the site's PHP container as www-data, in the site root.

app.name: App

app.uninstall_hint: The container and image are removed. Data is kept unless you also tick “remove data”.
app.uninstall_has_db: {n} database(s) still use this engine. Delete them on the Databases page first.

db.no_engine: No database engine is installed yet.

docker.name: Name
docker.ports_hint: One per line: [IP:]host:container[/udp]. Use 127.0.0.1: and bind a domain to publish through HTTPS.
docker.volumes_hint: Host folder (📁 to choose) or volume name, and the path inside the container
docker.project_delete_confirm: Stop project {name} and delete its files?
docker.prune_volumes: Remove volumes not used by any container?
docker.prune_networks: Remove networks not used by any container?

c.compose_owned: This container belongs to a Compose project; edit the project instead.

policy.always: Always restart, also after the Docker daemon restarts
policy.unless-stopped: Always restart, unless it was stopped by hand
policy.on-failure: Restart only when it exits with an error

c.commit_hint: Save the container's current filesystem as a new image (volumes are not included).
c.edit_hint: Saving recreates the container with these settings. Volumes and bind mounts are kept; if the new container fails to start, the old one is restored.
c.upgrade_hint: Pull a newer image (or another tag) and recreate the container with it, keeping its settings and volumes.
c.force_recreate: Recreate even if the image is unchanged
c.logs_hint: Shows the last 2,000 lines of the range; Download saves all of it.
c.no_ports: This container publishes no ports to the host. Add a port (e.g. 127.0.0.1:8080:80) in Edit container, then bind a domain here.
c.proxy_hint: Bind a domain to a published port: a reverse proxy website is created, with SSL if you choose.
c.none_bound: No domain is bound to this container yet.

files.name: Name
files.delete_confirm: Move {n} item(s) to the recycle bin?

files.resume_confirm: {name} was partly uploaded. Resume? (Cancel uploads it again)
files.empty_trash_confirm: Permanently delete everything in the recycle bin?

term.verify: Re-enter your panel password to open a root shell on this server.
term.verify_container: Re-enter your panel password to open a shell in {name}.

route.intro: Every hostname on ports 443/80 and where it goes. A hostname belongs to exactly one website, Docker binding or proxy; exact names win over wildcards, and a deeper wildcard over a shallower one.
route.warned: {n} hostname(s) need attention — hover the tags in the Checks column.

kind_hint.alias: Adds the hostname (e.g. a subdomain) to an existing site; request a certificate that covers it afterwards.
kind_hint.site: Creates a PHP, static, Node.js, Python or Java website for this hostname.
kind_hint.docker: Proxies HTTP to a port a container publishes on this server; HTTPS ends at the edge.
kind_hint.server: Reverse-proxies to another server or service: http(s)://host:port.
kind_hint.passthrough: Forwards the raw TLS stream by SNI to host:port; the backend holds the certificate.

match.default: No route for {host}: it gets the default certificate and nginx's default page.

no_cert.long: No valid certificate covers this hostname, so browsers see the default certificate. Request one under the site's SSL (wildcards need DNS-01).

cf_passthrough.long: Cloudflare's proxy (orange cloud) ends TLS itself, so the backend must present a certificate Cloudflare accepts; consider DNS only (grey cloud).

upstream_down.long: Nothing answers at the target address; the container or service may be stopped.

dns_none.long: The hostname does not resolve yet.

dns_elsewhere.long: The hostname resolves to an address that is not this server's public IP.

wildcard_overridden.long: These hostnames inside the wildcard belong to other sites: {hosts}

passthrough_realip.long: TLS is not ended here, so CF-Connecting-IP cannot be read: the backend only sees Cloudflare's addresses.

maint.update_desc: Download and install {to} (now {from}) from GitHub. The panel restarts for a moment.
maint.repair_desc: Reinstall the current version: program files, the systemd service and Docker are checked and rebuilt.
maint.kept: Kept: website files (/www), databases and app data, certificates, firewall rules, panel settings and accounts.
maint.rebuild: Also recreate the web stack containers (HAProxy, nginx, PHP-FPM) from the saved configuration
maint.wait: Running… the panel restarts during this, the log continues afterwards.
maint.failed: Failed (exit {code}); the installer rolled back to the previous version. See the log.
maint.rollback_desc: Go back from {from} to {to}, the version installed before the last update.
maint.with_data: Also restore the panel data backed up before that update (changes made since are kept aside)

geo.downloading: Downloading the IP database in the background…

cron.name: Name
cron.script_hint: Output and exit status are kept for each run; a run still going is skipped instead of starting twice.
cron.logrotate_hint: Gzips every website log in /www/wwwlogs and tells nginx to reopen them.

sys_hint.ssl_renew: Renews every website certificate that expires within 30 days.
sys_hint.time_sync: Restarts the NTP client (systemd-timesyncd), which corrects the clock.
sys_hint.release_memory: Writes caches to disk and drops the page cache; Linux refills it as files are read.
sys_hint.security_scan: Runs the security scan and raises an alert on critical findings.
sys_hint.app_updates: Checks installed software and PHP versions for patch updates and raises an alert; nothing is installed automatically.

cron.feeds_hint: Downloads the lists selected in Security → Auto-updated lists. Entries expire after two intervals if the task stops.
cron.mw_paths_hint: Under the website root; empty = every website

firewall.title: Firewall
firewall.desc: nftables on this server: default policy, ping and port rules.

ips.title: Black / white lists
ips.desc: IP, User-Agent and URL allow / block lists you add by hand. Automatic entries are under Cloud lists.

lists.title: Cloud lists
lists.desc: Entries added automatically: public block lists, trusted ranges (Cloudflare, search engines, AI crawlers), CrowdSec and AI bans.

cloud.title: Edge sync
cloud.desc: Push the manual block / allow lists to a Linode Cloud Firewall and Cloudflare.

waf.title: WAF
waf.desc: ModSecurity with the OWASP Core Rule Set in front of every website.

crowdsec.title: CrowdSec
crowdsec.desc: Reads the website and SSH logs, detects attacks and bans the attackers.

scan.title: Security scan
scan.desc: Checks SSH, accounts, updates, kernel settings, open ports and website permissions.

malware.title: Webshell scan
malware.desc: Finds webshells and suspicious code in the websites; quarantine or ignore each file.

tamper.title: Tamper protection
tamper.desc: Locks website directories, or watches them and undoes changes.

overview.title: Traffic overview
overview.desc: Every website together: requests, intercepted requests (WAF, rate limits, blocked clients), live load, visitors by country, clients and status codes.

protect.title: Site protection
protect.desc: Checks each website's requests go through at the edge (HAProxy): fake spiders, CDN only, data centres, scrapers, CC and dedicated rules.

rules.title: Dedicated rules
rules.desc: Rules against known CMS weaknesses (WordPress for now); switch, edit or add each one.

fw.title: Server firewall (nftables)
fw.enable_hint: Its own nftables table (inet lmcwhm); ufw and Docker rules are left alone. Rescue over SSH: lmcwhm firewall-off

policy_hint.accept: Everything is reachable except what rules and the block list deny.
policy_hint.drop: Only allow rules (including system rules) can connect. A 60-second safety check runs when applied.

fw.drop_unprotected: Drop policy with the SSH or panel system rule disabled: you can easily lock yourself out.
fw.confirming: Checking that the panel is still reachable through the new rules… reverts in {n} s if not.
fw.confirmed: The panel is reachable: new rules kept.
fw.confirm_failed: Could not reach the panel through the new rules: they are rolled back to Allow within {n} seconds.
fw.rules_hint: Evaluated in order after the block list. Allow rules matter with the Deny default; deny rules close a port with the Allow default.
fw.source_hint: Empty = anywhere; or an IP / CIDR (v4 or v6)
fw.live: Live ruleset (nft list table inet lmcwhm)
fw.no_nft: nftables (nft) is not installed: run install.sh again or apt install nftables.
fw.lists_hint: Allowed addresses skip every rule; blocked ones are dropped for all ports, also for Docker-published ports. Your own address cannot be blocked.
fw.lists_inactive: The firewall is off: lists are saved but not enforced on this server.
fw.sync_hint: Permanent blocks are pushed to the edges enabled under Linode / Cloudflare (automatically after changes). Temporary bans stay on the server.
fw.linode_intro: A Linode Cloud Firewall filters traffic before it reaches this server. Create a personal access token with Firewalls: Read/Write and Linodes: Read/Write.
fw.token_saved: Token saved (enter a new one to replace)
fw.linode_sync: Push the block list (a DROP rule labelled lmcwhm-block, first in order)
fw.linode_ports: Keep an ACCEPT rule for protected ports {ports} (lmcwhm-ports)
fw.linode_rules: {n} inbound rules, inbound default {policy}. Rules lmcwhm did not create are never changed.
fw.cf_no_token: Add a Cloudflare API token under Websites → Web stack to use Cloudflare.
fw.cf_sync: Push the block list to every zone as IP Access Rules (notes "lmcwhm")
fw.cf_hint: Cloudflare accepts single addresses, IPv4 /16 and /24 and IPv6 /32, /48 and /64. The token needs Zone → Firewall Services → Edit (and Zone → Zone Settings → Edit for the security level).
fw.synced_yes: Pushed to Linode / Cloudflare when sync is on
fw.synced_no: Server only (only permanent manual entries are synced)
fw.lists_hint2: Allowed addresses bypass every rule; blocked ones are dropped on all ports, Docker ports included. You cannot block your own address. Permanent entries added here are also the only ones synced to Linode / Cloudflare.
fw.sync_scope: Only the block and allow entries you add by hand (permanent ones) are pushed. Bans from CrowdSec, MCP and the public lists stay on this server: they change too often for the Linode and Cloudflare APIs.
fw.linode_sync2: Push the manual block and allow lists (lmcwhm-allow / lmcwhm-block rules, placed first)
fw.cf_sync2: Push the manual block and allow lists to every zone as IP Access Rules (note "lmcwhm")
fw.never_synced: Not synced yet. Turn on Linode or Cloudflare sync below; changes to the manual lists are pushed within seconds.
fw.ping_hint: When off, the server does not answer ICMP ping (IPv6 neighbour discovery still works).

sys.ssh: SSH — deleting or disabling it locks you out of SSH
sys.panel: Panel — deleting or disabling it locks you out of the panel

fw.sys_off_confirm: Disable a system rule? With a drop policy you may lock yourself out.
fw.sys_delete_confirm: Delete a system rule? It is not recreated, and with a drop policy you may lock yourself out.
fw.sys_ports: System rule ports follow the SSH and panel settings.

cdn.title: Real visitor IP behind a CDN
cdn.hint: Through a CDN (e.g. Cloudflare proxied), the server sees the CDN's address. Only requests from the CDN's ranges may set the visitor address from its header; logs, the WAF, CrowdSec, rate limits and the IP block list then use the real visitor address.
cdn.ranges_hint: One IP or CIDR per line; takes effect together with the header.

waf.title: Web application firewall
waf.enable_hint: ModSecurity v3 + OWASP Core Rule Set in nginx ({image}).
waf.anomaly_hint: Score at which a request is blocked (CRS default 5; higher = more permissive).
waf.sites_off: Turn the WAF on above for these settings to take effect.
waf.engine_hint: Applies to the OWASP rules only; each dedicated rule blocks or only detects on its own.

pl_hint.3: Strict: exclude false positives from the blocked log.
pl_hint.4: Very strict, for high-risk sites only.

waf.pl_rules: Dedicated rules active at this level: {n}.
waf.rules_switch_hint: Run at the edge (HAProxy), with or without OWASP; only rules at or below the paranoia level run.
waf.block_status_hint: What IP / UA / URL block lists and site protection answer (CC is always 429; dedicated rules set their own). 444 closes the connection.
waf.layers: Two layers: the edge (HAProxy) applies the lists, site protection and dedicated rules first, then the OWASP rules (ModSecurity) run in nginx. Both appear in the blocked log.

cs.intro: CrowdSec reads website and SSH logs, detects attacks (brute force, scans, CVE probes) and issues bans, which the panel enforces in its firewall.
cs.community: Join the community: share signals and receive the community blocklist
cs.uninstall_confirm: Remove CrowdSec and lift its bans?
cs.fw_off: The firewall is off: CrowdSec bans are recorded but not enforced. Enable it under Firewall.
cs.community_empty: The community blocklist is still empty. CrowdSec only sends it to engines that share signals, and this server has not detected an attack yet, so it has nothing to share. It fills in once attacks are detected. Until then, subscribe to the public blocklists below.

bk.delete_confirm: Delete this backup (also on the cloud storage)?

bk.exclude_hint: File or folder name patterns, e.g. node_modules, *.log, cache
bk.plan_name_hint: Optional; defaults to the type and target
bk.cron_hint: Backup plan as JSON; easier to edit on the Backups page.

restore_warn.site: The files of {target} will be replaced by this backup. The current files are swapped out only after the archive unpacked completely.

restore_warn.volume: Everything in volume {target} is deleted and replaced. Stop the containers that use it first.
restore_warn.path: Directory {target} will be replaced by this backup.

bk.import_hint: Upload the archive with the file manager first (e.g. from another server), then register it here so it can be restored.
bk.remote_intro: Backups can be uploaded to Google Drive or OneDrive. You register your own OAuth app, then approve the panel with a one-time code; no callback URL to the panel is needed.

howto.onedrive: Azure portal → App registrations → New registration (personal and/or work accounts). Under Authentication enable “Allow public client flows”. Paste the Application (client) ID here. Files go to the app folder Apps/<app name>.

bk.remote_delete_confirm: Remove this storage? Its backups stay in the cloud but disappear from the list.
bk.authorize_step1: 1. Open this page and sign in:
bk.authorize_wait: This window closes by itself once you approve.
bk.auth_expired: The code expired or was declined; try again.

ai.no_key: Add an Anthropic API key to use the assistant.
ai.intro: Ask about this server. The assistant reads logs, metrics and settings through read-only tools and tells you what to do; it does not change anything.
ai.placeholder: e.g. Why is example.com returning 502? (Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line)

security.label: Security triage
security.prompt: Do a security triage of this server: firewall, SSH and panel logins, WAF and CrowdSec events, suspicious requests. Rank the risks and tell me what to fix.

load.label: Why is it slow?
load.prompt: Investigate CPU, memory, disk and network usage over the last 24 hours and tell me what is causing load.

backups.label: Check backups
backups.prompt: Review backup coverage: which sites and databases have no recent or off-site backup, and which backup jobs fail?

errors.label: Find website errors
errors.prompt: Check every website for 5xx errors, error log entries and stopped containers, and explain the causes.

ai.prompt_ssh: Analyse the recent SSH logins: brute-force sources, unusual successful logins, and whether I should block anything.
ai.prompt_site_access: Analyse the access log of {domain}: traffic, errors, top clients and suspicious requests.
ai.prompt_site_error: Read the error log of {domain} and explain each problem and its fix.
ai.prompt_site_traffic: Summarise the traffic of {domain} and point out anything unusual (bots, attacks, error spikes).
ai.prompt_waf: Review the recent WAF events: which are real attacks and which look like false positives? Propose rule exclusions per site.
ai.connect_ssh: Over SSH (no token, uses your SSH login; recommended):
ai.connect_http: Over HTTPS with an API token (the panel port must be reachable; a self-signed certificate must be trusted by the client):

scope_hint.read: Read logs, metrics and settings only.
scope_hint.operate: Also restart containers, block IPs, run cron jobs and backups, issue certificates.
scope_hint.admin: Also run any shell command as root. Give it only to clients you fully trust.

ai.ips_hint: Empty = any IP (the panel's own IP restriction still applies)
ai.revoke_confirm: Revoke this token? Clients using it stop working.
ai.token_once: Copy it now: it is shown only once.
ai.api_key_hint: From console.anthropic.com; stored encrypted. Usage is billed to your account.
ai.model_hint: Default {model}; a Sonnet or Haiku model costs less.
ai.effort_hint: Higher is more thorough but slower and costs more.
ai.base_url_hint: Only for a gateway in front of the Anthropic API.

risks.no_entry: No security entry: the login page is reachable by anyone who finds the port.
risks.default_port: The panel uses the default port 8888.
risks.panel_http: Panel SSL is off: logins travel unencrypted.
risks.panel_open: No authorised IPs or BasicAuth in front of the panel.
risks.no_2fa: Two-factor authentication is off for the admin.
risks.no_recent_backup: No backup in the last 7 days.
risks.no_alert_channel: No alert channel: you will not be notified of problems.
risks.cron_failed: {n} cron job(s) failed on their last run.

adv.title: Advanced
adv.allow_ips_hint: When set, every other IP gets 403. IPs or CIDRs.
adv.deny_ua_hint: Case-insensitive parts of the User-Agent, e.g. MJ12bot, python-requests
adv.hotlink_hint: Domains allowed to embed images and media; empty = off. Your own domains are always allowed.
adv.rate_hint: 0 = no limit; over the limit returns 429.
adv.error_pages: Custom error pages (/404.html, /50x.html in the site root)
adv.varnish_ttl_hint: For pages without their own Cache-Control. Logged-in users, POSTs, admin pages and responses that set cookies are never cached.

stats.title: Traffic
stats.spiders_excluded: {n} crawler requests are counted in PV but not in UV or the top lists.

wp.install_intro: Install WordPress into this site: a MySQL / MariaDB database is created, wp-config.php is written and the admin user is set up with WP-CLI.
wp.need_mysql: Install MySQL or MariaDB from the App Store first.
wp.no_file_edit: Disable the dashboard plugin / theme editor (DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT)

php.remove_confirm: Remove this PHP container? Its settings are kept.
php.hint: Each PHP version runs as its own PHP-FPM container; a version starts automatically when a website uses it.
php.ext_hint: Ticked extensions are compiled into an image layer for this version (install-php-extensions). Saving rebuilds it, which can take several minutes; the running version keeps serving until the new one passes its test.
php.disable_hint: PHP code cannot call these functions (disable_functions). WP-CLI and Composer run through the CLI and are not affected.
php.custom_hint: Extra php.ini lines appended after the settings above, e.g. extension options. The whole configuration is tested with php-fpm -t before it is applied.
php.in_use_count: {n} website(s) use this version; switch them to another version first.

varnish.hint: Turn the cache on per website under Website → Settings → Advanced. Varnish runs only while a site uses it.

api.intro: Every route the panel uses. Call them with an API token: Authorization: Bearer lmc_… (read tokens: GET only; operate: every module except panel administration; admin: everything). Long operations return a task_id to poll at GET /tasks/{id}.

scan.weekly: The panel also scans weekly and alerts on critical findings (Alerts → Security scan).
scan.ai_prompt: Explain these security scan findings for my server and tell me what to fix first:

risks.ssh_root_login: root may log in over SSH
risks.ssh_default_port: SSH listens on the default port 22
risks.ssh_max_auth_tries: SSH allows many password attempts per connection
risks.reboot_required: A reboot is needed to finish updates (new kernel)
risks.sysctl: Kernel network / memory hardening is not applied
risks.docker_api_exposed: The Docker API is reachable from the network
risks.php_eol: Websites run PHP versions without security support
risks.php_in_uploads: PHP files in WordPress uploads (often a webshell)

fix_confirm.ssh_root: Allow root to log in with SSH keys only?
fix_confirm.apt_upgrade: Install all package updates now (apt-get upgrade)?
fix_confirm.auto_updates: Install unattended-upgrades and turn on automatic security updates?
fix_confirm.lock_empty: Lock the accounts that have no password?
fix_confirm.chmod_web: Remove write permission for others from every file in the website folders?

scan.how_route: Open the related page and change the setting.

mw.hint: Signature rules for PHP / JSP / ASP webshells and code hidden in images. Check a file before deleting it: some plugins legitimately use eval or base64. Ignore whitelists the exact content.
mw.quarantine_confirm: Move this file out of the website (it can be restored)?
mw.clamav: Also scan with ClamAV (first run downloads ~300 MB of signatures, needs ~1.5 GB RAM)

rules.write_input: writes request input to a file

tp.intro: Watch mode reports every change to protected files and can undo it (new files are moved aside). Lock mode makes them immutable: nothing, not even PHP or root, can change them until the rule is off — turn it off before updating the site.

mode_hint.watch: inotify watches the folder; with Restore on, changed or deleted files are put back from a baseline copy taken now.
mode_hint.lock: Sets the immutable attribute (chattr +i) on protected files and folders. Excluded folders stay writable.

tp.exclude_hint: Relative to the folder, e.g. wp-content/uploads

users.intro: Operator accounts for the panel (not hosting customers): each sees only the modules ticked here, optionally only some websites. Administrators can do everything.
users.keep_password: Leave empty to keep the current password
users.sites_hint: When set, the user manages only these sites; modules that reach the whole server (files, terminal, Docker, ...) are then unavailable.
users.root_warning: Files and Terminal act as root on the server: only grant them to people you would give the root password.

dns.no_token: Add a Cloudflare API token (Website → Environment) with Zone: DNS Edit permission to edit DNS here.
dns.name: Name
dns.template_hint: Existing identical records are skipped; an existing SPF or DMARC record is replaced (a name may only have one).

fx.truncated: Showing the first results only; narrow the folder or the query.
fx.share_hint: 0 = no limit. Anyone with the link can download this file (the panel's IP allow-list still applies).

tb.swap_hint: The swap file is /swapfile; 0 removes it.
tb.dns_resolved: Set through systemd-resolved; empty = back to the DHCP servers.
tb.tz_hint: The panel's own timezone (logs, cron) is under Settings.
tb.ssh_port_hint: The panel firewall opens the new port first; also open it in a cloud firewall you manage elsewhere.
tb.lockout: Turn on password or key login (with a key added below), or nobody can log in.
tb.ssh_confirm: Restart SSH with these settings? Keep this session open until you have tested a new login.
tb.name: Name

mail.disable_confirm: Stop the mail server? Mailboxes and keys are kept.
mail.intro: docker-mailserver (Postfix, Dovecot, OpenDKIM, Fail2ban) on ports {ports}. Use a hostname such as mail.example.com: add it as a website and issue SSL first so mail uses TLS. Open these ports in your cloud firewall; many providers block outbound port 25 until you ask.
mail.domain_delete: Remove this domain? Delete its mailboxes first.
mail.account_delete: Delete this mailbox and its mail?
mail.client_hint: Mail clients: IMAP {host}:993 (SSL), SMTP {host}:465 (SSL) or 587 (STARTTLS); username = full address.
mail.ptr_hint: Also set the server IP's reverse DNS (PTR) to the mail hostname at your VPS provider (e.g. Linode → Network → Reverse DNS).

fwfeed.title: Public malicious IP blocklists
fwfeed.intro: Downloaded on a schedule and blocked by the panel firewall; works without CrowdSec. Private ranges, this server's addresses, the allow list and IPs that logged into the panel in the last 30 days are never blocked. Entries expire by themselves if a list stops updating.
fwfeed.custom: Custom lists (one IP or CIDR per line; always on)
fwfeed.name: Name
fwfeed.no_job: created when you select a list
fwfeed.job_disabled: The scheduled task is disabled: the lists are not updated and their entries will expire.

fwtrust.title: Trusted IPs (auto-updated)
fwtrust.intro: Cloudflare and search engine / AI crawler ranges, downloaded on a schedule. Trusted IPs are never blocked or banned: not by CrowdSec, malicious IP lists or manual blocks. They are not opened to every port: port rules and the default policy still apply, because anyone can send traffic from Cloudflare (Workers) and fully allowing it would expose SSH and databases. Yahoo uses Bing's crawler; Sogou and 360 publish no IP lists.

dbs.oom_hint: Lowers the OOM score so the kernel kills other processes first when memory runs out, keeping this database up. Other services may be killed instead; turn it on only where this database matters most. Applying it recreates the container (a short restart).
dbs.config_hint_my: Overrides merged over the image's my.cnf. Saving restarts the server; if it does not come back, the previous file is restored.
dbs.config_hint_redis: redis.conf of this instance. Saving restarts Redis; if it does not come back, the previous file is restored. Do not change bind or port here: use the Port setting.
dbs.port_hint: The service listens on 127.0.0.1 only. Websites and apps that connect to the old port must be updated; phpMyAdmin is updated automatically.

tip.connections: If the peak is close to max_connections, raise max_connections
tip.open_tables: table_open_cache should be at least this
tip.full_join: If not 0, check the tables' indexes
tip.range_check: If not 0, check the tables' indexes
tip.locks_waited: If high, consider InnoDB instead of MyISAM

dbs.redis_note: Applied live without a restart (data stays in memory), except the number of databases, which restarts Redis. Redis only listens on 127.0.0.1: never publish it to the internet.
dbs.fsync_hint: everysec: at most one second of writes lost
dbs.rdb_hint: A snapshot is taken when any rule matches; no rules = snapshots off.
dbs.binlog_hint: Binary logs record every change, for point-in-time recovery and replication; they can grow large. Turning them on or off restarts the server.

rk.flush_confirm: Delete every key in DB{db}? This cannot be undone.

apis.intro: Every third-party API key the panel uses, in one place. Keys are stored encrypted and never shown again.
apis.moved: The Cloudflare API token is now managed in Panel settings → API credentials.
apis.cf_used: Used for DNS records, DNS-01 certificates (wildcards) and Cloudflare firewall sync.
apis.linode_used: Used for the Linode Cloud Firewall (Security → Cloud sync).
apis.linode_hint: Personal access token with Firewalls: Read/Write and Linodes: Read/Write. Saving checks it first.
apis.linode_ok: Token works; this server is Linode {name}
apis.ai_used: Used by the AI assistant and the AI analysis buttons.

tr.blocked_hint: Addresses whose requests were intercepted most; click one to block it in the firewall.
tr.visit_hint: Countries of the top visitor IPs ({n} requests).
tr.status_hint: 403, 429 and 444 are intercepted requests: WAF, rate limits and blocked user agents.

ce.keys: Ctrl/⌘+S save · Ctrl/⌘+F find and replace · Ctrl/⌘+Alt+G go to line

fp.title: Choose a folder
fp.name: Name
fp.hint: Click a folder to select it, double-click to open it.
fp.hint_file: Click a file to select it; double-click a folder to open it.

hint.ip_allow: Allowed IPs are not limited by any firewall rule.
hint.ip_block: Blocked IPs are dropped on every port; through a CDN they are refused at the website edge by the real address (403). The firewall must be on.
hint.ua_allow: Requests with a matching User-Agent skip the UA / URL block lists and the WAF.
hint.ua_block: Requests with a matching User-Agent are refused (403) on every website, with or without the firewall.
hint.url_allow: Requests to a matching URL skip the UA / URL block lists and the WAF (e.g. webhooks, APIs).
hint.url_block: Requests whose URL (path + query) matches are refused (403) on every website.

fwl.clear_confirm: Remove all {n} entries of this list?
fwl.import_hint: One per line; lines starting with # are skipped
fwl.remove_auto: Remove {ip}? The next list update may add it again.
fwl.auto_hint: Only automatic entries are shown here. "Keep as manual" turns a block entry into a permanent manual block.

tips.fake_spider: A User-Agent claiming a search engine or AI crawler from outside its official ranges is refused. Only crawlers whose trusted list is on (Cloud lists → Sources) are checked.
tips.cdn_only: Only requests through a CDN (Cloudflare or the CDN you set) are accepted, so nobody can bypass it by calling the server's IP. Turn on only for proxied sites.
tips.idc: Refuse cloud and hosting addresses (AWS, Azure, Alibaba, Tencent, DigitalOcean, …), except trusted crawlers and allowed IPs. Needs the GeoIP ASN database.
tips.crawler: Refuse common scraper and bad-bot User-Agents (python-requests, curl, Scrapy, AhrefsBot, …); the list is under Protection settings.
tips.cc: Most requests a visitor IP may make in 10 seconds; over it gets 429. 0 = off.
tips.waf: OWASP rules (ModSecurity) on this site; turn the WAF on first.

prot.no_spiders: Fake spider is on but no trusted crawler list is, so nothing is refused. Turn on Googlebot, Bingbot, Baidu, … under Cloud lists → Sources.
prot.no_asn: No IDC is on but the ASN database is missing: download it under Logs → GeoIP.
prot.note_order: Order: IP block list → UA / URL block lists → CDN only → fake spider → no IDC → scrapers → dedicated rules → CC. Allowed IPs and UA / URL allow lists skip site protection.
prot.note_cdn: Behind Cloudflare the real visitor IP is used (Firewall → Real visitor IP). Passthrough sites end TLS elsewhere, so this does not apply to them.
prot.note_count: Blocked counts come from the site logs (403 / 429), updated every hour.
prot.crawlers_hint: One User-Agent fragment per line (refused when contained, any case).
prot.idc_hint: One AS number and name per line, e.g. 16509 Amazon AWS. {n} ranges now.
prot.bad_asn: Each line must start with an AS number
prot.excl_hint: CRS rule IDs not run on this site (e.g. a false positive 942100).

rules.title: Dedicated rules
rules.name: Name
rules.reset_confirm: Restore the default conditions and switch?
rules.off_hint: The dedicated rules switch is off: the rules below do nothing. Once on they apply to every site with protection on; switch off a rule that blocks too much.
rules.note_scope: With the switch on, rules apply to every website with site protection on; switch off a single rule if it refuses legitimate requests.
rules.note_log: Refused requests get 403 and show a reason such as "rule wp-1002" under Site protection → Blocked log.
rules.values_hint: A condition can have several values; any one matching is enough. Press Enter after each. Matching ignores case.
rules.code_hint: The conditions as JSON: field (path / url / query / method / ua / referer / cookie / body), op (contains / equals / prefix / suffix / regex), negate, values.

dom.intro: One row per domain (its aliases and subdomains with it). Manage sets where it goes (a website, Docker, a URL, passthrough, a redirect), its aliases, SSL and DNS; a website's own PHP, runtime and rewrite settings stay in the website settings.

target_hint.site: This domain's own website files / project.
target_hint.link: Shows another website's content (a website can have several domains, each with its SSL).
target_hint.docker: Goes to a port a container publishes (TLS ends at the edge, then HTTP).
target_hint.url: Reverse proxy to any http(s) URL, e.g. a server on the private network.
target_hint.passthrough: The TLS stream goes untouched to host:port (the backend holds the certificate; the CDN visitor IP cannot be read).
target_hint.redirect: Every request is redirected to another URL.

dom.retarget_note: This domain's website files ({root}) are kept; switch back to "Its website" to serve them again.
dom.aliases_hint: Press Enter after each; wildcards like *.example.com work.
dom.ssl_passthrough: TLS passthrough: the backend holds the certificate, nothing to issue here.
dom.dns_hint: When on, the panel creates and updates the A / AAAA records of this domain and every alias in Cloudflare.
dom.delete_confirm: Delete {host}? Its Cloudflare DNS records are removed too.

add_hint.entry: Next, choose where it goes: another website, Docker, a URL, passthrough or a redirect.
add_hint.alias: An alias of an existing domain, with the same target and SSL.
add_hint.site: A new website with its own files (PHP, static, Node.js, …).

dom.drawer_hint: Domains, aliases, SSL, DNS and the target now live on the Domains / SNI page; change them here with Manage domain.
dom.not_serving: This domain now goes to another service

fwd.title: Port forwarding
fwd.note_proto: TCP, UDP or both; the visitor IP is kept (to a local port).
fwd.note_firewall: The firewall lets forwarded connections through; with a Linode Cloud Firewall, open the listen port there too.
fwd.note_remote: Forwarding to another server is IPv4 only and masqueraded (it sees this server as the source).

crs.unavailable: The rules are listed when the WAF (OWASP) is on and nginx is running.
crs.hint: Rules switched off for all sites never run ({n} now); "exclude on a site" skips a rule on that site only. Greyed levels are above the paranoia level and do not run.

ep.intercept: Replace the backend's own error pages (PHP / project / proxy) too
ep.site_hint: This site only; "inherit" uses the default above.
ep.global_hint: The default for every site; each site can override it. A site with "custom error pages" on keeps its own 404.html / 50x.html.

menucfg.title: Main menu
menucfg.hint: Drag or use ↑↓ to reorder; the switch shows or hides an entry. Home and Panel settings always show; hidden pages still open by their address.

fm.copied_n: {n} item(s) copied: paste them in the target folder
fm.cut_n: {n} item(s) cut: paste them in the target folder
fm.hint: Click to select, double-click to open; right-click (or long-press) for more; click the empty part of the path to type one; click a remark to edit it.

fe.title: Online text editor
fe.none: Pick a file on the left
fe.discard_all: Some files have unsaved changes. Discard and close?
fe.restore_confirm: Restore this version? The current content is kept as a version too.
fe.history_hint: The previous content is kept each time you save in the editor (10 versions per file).

up.title: Upload to {dir} (resumable)
up.partial: The server has {have} of {want}: it can resume.

rb.warn: Off: deleted files are removed for good at once
rb.db_warn: Off: dropped databases are not kept
rb.off_confirm: Switch the recycle bin off? Deleted files will be removed for good.
rb.db_off_confirm: Switch the database bin off? Dropped databases will not be kept.
rb.name: Name
rb.db_hint: Databases dropped in the panel are dumped here first; restoring creates the database, user and password again.

ss.title: Website settings [{domain}]
ss.hosts_ph:
One domain per line, e.g.
www.example.com
wildcard: *.example.com
ss.hosts_hint: Domains added here share the website's SSL and settings. SSL, DNS and targets are managed on the Domains page.
ss.subdir_hint: The domain then serves that directory of this website (same PHP and settings).
ss.run_dir_hint: Some apps serve a subdirectory, e.g. /public for Laravel
ss.basedir_hint: open_basedir: PHP may only open the website root and /tmp
ss.access_log_hint: Off: no access log, and no website statistics
ss.password_hint: Visitors must enter a user name and password
ss.dir_auth_hint: These paths ask for a password (e.g. /admin/).
ss.name: Name
ss.server_conn_hint: Most connections for the whole site
ss.rw_hint1: If the website breaks after choosing a template, switch back to default
ss.rw_hint2: nginx -t checks the rules before they apply.
ss.index_hint: Index files, one per line, first match wins
ss.custom_hint: Custom directives go inside the server {'{'} {'}'} block (add_header, location…). Other panel settings never overwrite them; nginx -t checks them first.
ss.redirect_hint: Path redirects: the path on the left goes to the URL on the right.
ss.redirect_domain: To redirect a whole domain, set its target to Redirect on the Domains page.
ss.proxy_hint: Forward a path to another service, e.g. /api/ → http://127.0.0.1:3000.
ss.hl_empty_label: Allow requests without a Referer (opened directly)
ss.no_perm: You do not have access to this part
ss.tamper_hint: Tamper protection watches the website files and undoes or blocks changes.
ss.tamper_create: Protect this website (watch and undo PHP / JS / HTML)
ss.uptime_hint: Checks {url} every minute; failures go to the alert center.
ss.expiry_hint: The website stops on that day (with an alert); empty = never.
ss.ssl_alert_hint: Certificates renew themselves; expiry alerts are set in the alert center.

sb.title: Backups of {domain}
sb.hint: Schedules and remote storage are set on the Backup page.

ws.overview_hint: Today; click a website for its report.
ws.name: Website
ws.stop_page_hint: Pages are edited under WAF → Error pages.
ws.delete_files: Delete the website files too (to the recycle bin)
ws.delete_hint: Databases and FTP accounts stay; remove them on their pages.

bm.title: Install method
bm.fast_hint: The official pre-built image: done in a minute or two, the most tested.
bm.source_hint: The same version compiled on this server, with your own options. About {n} minutes on 2 cores; needs {mem} MB of memory (with swap).
bm.warn: Compiling uses all CPU cores. The current version keeps running and is only replaced once the build works; a failure rolls back.
bm.args_hint: Added to ./configure (or cmake / make), e.g. --enable-xxx. No quotes or $.
bm.switch_hint: Data, settings and ports stay; databases are backed up first.

no.huge: MongoDB needs ~40 GB of disk and hours to compile: not offered.
no.jdk: The JDK build needs another JDK and many hours: not offered.
no.bytecode: Tomcat is Java bytecode: nothing to compile.
no.closed: SQL Server has no public source.
no.script: A PHP application: nothing to compile.
no.old: MySQL 5.7 is end-of-life: no compile install.
no.none: No compile install for this app.
